title: Convertible ships a tui command whose every visual frame has an agent-readable semantic mirror (TJSON), so a coder agent can read, operate, snapshot, replay, and diagnose the terminal UI without OCR or terminal guessing.

targets.text: Convertible ships a tui command whose every visual frame has an agent-readable semantic mirror (TJSON), so a coder agent can read, operate, snapshot, replay, and diagnose the terminal UI without OCR or terminal guessing.
A captured frame round-trips: state -> TJSON -> replay/render reproduces the same frame, and the TJSON mirror is complete enough that diagnose never needs OCR or terminal scraping.
Coder agents (Codex, Claude Code, convertible's own engines) that must read, operate, and debug the TUI — and the humans who use it interactively.
The TJSON payload is consumable by a coder agent with no convertible-specific client (plain JSON over stdout/file), and a human can run the same 'tui' and see the rendered frame.

Every meaningful visual TUI frame has a structured TJSON mirror an agent can read, inspect by stable selector, operate (selector->event), snapshot, replay deterministically, and diagnose — no OCR, no terminal key-sequence guessing.
Each of read/inspect/operate/snapshot/replay/diagnose maps to a concrete 'tui' subcommand that works headless, with no real terminal attached.

Terminal UIs are opaque to agents: an agent can run a TUI but cannot reliably know what state it is in, what action is available, why a popup appeared, whether focus is correct, or whether the visual frame disagrees with app state.
Without TJSON the same bug can only be reported by pasting ANSI/screenshots; with it the agent names the failing selector and bug class from structured data.
It moves the TUI from a blind spot inside the agent workflow into part of it: a human-seen bug becomes an agent-diagnosable snapshot, repairable via deterministic replay.
A human-captured snapshot triple is sufficient input for an agent to diagnose and propose a fix offline, without reproducing the bug live.
Not a daemon/server, not a new parallel runtime (foreground TTY like session), not a base TUI-library dependency, and not an LLM-based diagnose. The live TTY driver is the thinnest, last slice.
No code path in the tui feature opens a socket, forks a daemon, adds a base dependency, or calls a model; the live driver is a foreground process that exits on quit.
A coder agent reconstructs TUI state from an events.jsonl via the pure reducer and classifies a TUI bug from the snapshot triple, with no real terminal attached and no model call.
A passing CI test feeds an events.jsonl to the reducer and asserts diagnose's bug-class output, running with no TTY and no network.

The reducer is a pure function reduce(state, event) -> state: no I/O, no clock, no randomness. Determinism (incl. --animations=deterministic) comes from advancing the animation frame only via explicit injected 'tick' events, never by reading wall-clock time.
The animation frame counter is a field in State advanced only by a tick event; two replays of the same events.jsonl produce byte-identical ANSI.

TJSON is serialize(state): a single derived mirror of canonical State, never hand-maintained beside the renderer. Stable selectors are dotted JSON-paths into that TJSON tree (e.g. popup.skill.boost.accept), so they cannot drift from state.
Renaming or moving a node in State changes both its render and its selector path in lockstep; there is no second selector table that can disagree.

The base install stays zero-deps (dependencies = []): the tui core (state/reducer/tjson/selectors/snapshot/replay/diagnose) never imports a rendering library; only the optional [tui] renderer wheel may. Guarded by test_zero_deps.
After installing only the base package (no extras), importing convertible.cockpit/tui modules introduces no third-party module, asserted by test_zero_deps; the ANSI default renderer still works.
No visual-only truth: every meaningful state lives in TJSON as data (e.g. status.severity), and colour/animation/theme only reflects it. An agent reads severity, never a colour.

For a state with status.severity='error', the TJSON carries severity='error' and a message string; the red background is derivable from severity, and removing colour loses no information an agent needs.

diagnose is a pure stdlib cross-mirror differ: it folds events.jsonl through the reducer, compares against the captured .tjson and greps the .ansi, and classifies the disagreement into the 7 bug classes (state/render/layout/focus/input-routing/theme/popup-lifecycle) — no LLM, no tokens.
Given a snapshot triple where TJSON says popup visible=true but the ANSI lacks the popup title, diagnose returns 'render bug' (not state/layout) using only stdlib string/JSON comparison.

acceptance_criteria: CockpitState.to_dict()/from_dict() round-trip to an identical object
State holds screen, mode, focused, zones, panels, popups, background (with an integer animation 'frame' field), status (severity+message strings as data), drive, and problems
Each event type (user_input, key, tick, skill_suggested, dismiss, drive_step) round-trips through to_dict/from_dict and one-event-per-line JSONL
reduce() imports no os/time/random and reads no clock (purity asserted by test)
reduce(state, tick) advances only background.frame by a fixed delta; reduce(state, skill_suggested(boost)) opens popup.skill.boost; reduce(state, dismiss) closes it

tasks.summary: convertible/tui/taui.py: serialize(state) -> TAUI mirror dict + SCHEMA_VERSION
acceptance_criteria: serialize(state) returns a plain json.dumps-able dict; every popup/panel/action node carries a stable 'id'; status.severity+message present as data
the dict is consumable with no convertible import (pure JSON), and carries taui_version

tasks.summary: convertible/tui/render/ansi.py + widgets/ (status_bar, skill_panel, conversation, prompt_input, popup_layer): render(state)->str
acceptance_criteria: render(state) returns an ANSI string; a visible popup's title appears in the text; status.severity='error' renders red SGR codes yet the message text is still present (colour is reflection, not the only carrier)

tasks.summary: convertible/tui/selectors.py: resolve a dotted-path selector into the TAUI tree -> node/Action + selector->event
acceptance_criteria: resolve(taui, 'popup.skill.boost.accept') returns the action node; an unknown selector raises a clean error; a selector path is computed from the tree (moving a node changes its path) — there is no second selector table
snapshot.write(name, state, events) produces exactly the 3 files; read() reconstructs taui+ansi+events; the triple alone is sufficient input (no live process needed)

tasks.summary: convertible/tui/replay.py: fold an events.jsonl through reduce() -> state, deterministically
acceptance_criteria: replay(events) reconstructs the final state; replaying the same events.jsonl twice yields byte-identical ANSI (deterministic, no clock)

tasks.summary: convertible/tui/diagnose.py: pure stdlib cross-mirror differ -> classify the 7 bug classes
acceptance_criteria: given a triple where TAUI says popup visible=true but the ANSI lacks the title, diagnose returns 'render bug' (not state/layout)
diagnose classifies all 7 classes (state/render/layout/focus/input-routing/theme/popup-lifecycle), imports no model/network module, and a CI test exercises events->reducer->diagnose with no TTY

tasks.summary: convertible/cli/_commands/tui.py + register in cli/__init__.py + explain catalog entry + scenario test: headless subcommands (render --state, state, snapshot, replay, inspect --select, action --select, test --scenario, diagnose, overview)
acceptance_criteria: every listed subcommand runs headless (no TTY) with --json, errors via CliError, and 'tui overview' + an explain catalog entry exist
a scenario YAML (scenarios/boost-popup.yaml) drives skill_suggested->popup and a test asserts the resulting TAUI + ANSI expectations

tasks.summary: pyproject.toml: optional [tui] extra (Rich/Textual) + 'convertible.renderers' entry-point group (ansi default registered); update tests/test_zero_deps.py + docs/features/tui.md
acceptance_criteria: base install keeps dependencies = []; importing the convertible.tui core (state/events/reducer/taui/selectors/snapshot/replay/diagnose) introduces no third-party module, asserted by test_zero_deps; the default ANSI renderer still works
the [tui] extra and convertible.renderers entry-point group are declared; no tui code path opens a socket, forks a daemon, or calls a model

tasks.summary: convertible/tui/render/driver.py: live foreground TTY loop (termios raw mode) + wire 'tui' (no subcommand) default func in cli/_commands/tui.py
acceptance_criteria: running 'tui' starts a foreground loop that reads keys, routes them via selectors->events->reduce, repaints the ANSI frame, and exits cleanly on quit (no daemon, no socket); the driver is the only impure seam

risks.text: Live TTY driver raw-mode input handling (termios/tty): keymap->event routing test strategy is TBD; the driver is intentionally the last/thinnest slice.
Rich/Textual renderer wheel + populated convertible.renderers group ship after the stdlib-ANSI MVP; v0 ships only the default ANSI renderer.
Whether 'convertible session' folds into 'tui' (tui as full-screen session) or stays a separate verb — decide post-MVP.
